Project fit

Expand Your Living Space With a Well-Planned Home Addition

When your home no longer fits your life, a well-planned addition adds the space you need without starting over. RT Signature Homes coordinates design, structure, and finishes so new bedrooms, living areas, or suites feel like a natural part of the house and support how your household lives.

Typical scope

  • Feasibility, zoning, setback, and lot-coverage review
  • Architectural and structural integration
  • Foundation, framing, roofing, siding, windows, and utilities
  • Interior connection, circulation, and finish continuity
  • Permitting, inspections, and construction sequencing

Why choose us

Why Choose Us for Your Home Addition Project

Improves the existing rooms

A home additions project succeeds when it improves the rooms it touches, so we study the existing floor plan before drawing a new wall.

Coordinated early

Structure, utilities, and rooflines are coordinated early, which keeps the new space from forcing awkward compromises inside the home.

Feasibility first

We start with feasibility and setbacks rather than assumptions, so you learn what the property supports before investing in a full design.

Design ideas

Expand Your Living Room With a Thoughtfully Designed Room Addition

A thoughtfully designed room addition can open up cramped living areas and give your family room to spread out. The right design brings in daylight, improves flow, and makes the expanded space feel intentional.

Home Addition Design Ideas

Explore bump-outs, great-room expansions, and connected living spaces, with massing, rooflines, openings, and material transitions planned so old and new feel like one home.

Explore the gallery

Exterior integration

Design a Home Addition That Complements Your Property's Architecture

An addition should look like it was always part of the house, so we design it to respect the proportions, rooflines, and weather-protection strategy of the existing home.

Roof pitch, eave lines, siding, window styles, and trim are matched carefully, and roof drainage, flashing, and foundation connections are detailed as part of the design rather than left as cleanup.

Whether it is a main-floor bump-out, a second-story addition, or a new primary suite, the goal is an exterior that reads as original to your property's architecture.

Interior connection

Improve Your Home's Layout With a Seamlessly Integrated Room Addition

The best additions improve the rooms they touch, so we plan the connection between old and new around circulation, daylight, and how you move through the home.

The opening between existing and added space is designed to keep sightlines, flow, and furniture placement comfortable, with heating, cooling, and electrical capacity accounted for from the start.

A seamlessly integrated room addition solves the larger layout problem rather than simply attaching square footage, so the whole floor plan works better.

How the work moves

A process that keeps decisions ahead of construction.

Discovery and site assessment

We clarify goals, review existing conditions, identify constraints, and determine what needs deeper investigation before a scope is written.

Design and pre-construction

Layout, materials, trade requirements, permits, allowances, schedule factors, and decision deadlines are coordinated into one buildable plan.

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

Budget and schedule orientation

Scope the variables before suggesting a number.

Useful early guidance identifies what changes the investment and timeline. A responsible project range follows an assessment of the property, scope, finish expectations, and delivery constraints.

Common factors

  • Existing structural and mechanical conditions
  • Project size, layout changes, and finish level
  • Permit, engineering, and design requirements
  • Material availability and product lead times
  • Site access, protection, and project sequencing

Questions homeowners ask

Home Additions FAQs

What is the difference between a room addition and a home addition?

A room addition typically creates one specific space, such as a bedroom, office, or family room. A home addition is a broader term that can include one room or multiple connected spaces designed to expand the existing home's footprint.

Can I add a bedroom without making my existing living areas feel smaller?

Yes, a well-planned bedroom addition can create extra space while preserving the functionality of your current rooms. The design should consider the property's available space, access points, natural lighting, and how the new room will connect to the existing layout.

What should I consider before adding a second story to my home?

A second-story addition requires careful evaluation of the existing foundation, structural framing, roof, and load-bearing elements. Building codes, stair placement, utility changes, and the project's effect on existing rooms should also be assessed before finalizing the design.

Can a home addition include a bathroom or expanded kitchen?

Yes, a home addition can incorporate a bathroom, kitchen expansion, or other functional living areas. These projects may require plumbing, electrical, ventilation, and structural modifications, so coordinating the layout and utility requirements early is important.

How can I make a new home addition look like part of the original house?

Matching rooflines, exterior materials, window styles, trim, flooring transitions, and interior finishes can help create a cohesive appearance. Careful planning of room connections, ceiling heights, and natural light also helps the new space feel integrated rather than added on later.
